'''Numanggang''' (Manggang) is a language of [[Papua New Guinea]]. Other names are Boana, Kai, Ngain, Sugu. Numanggang is preferred over [[Tok Pisin]] in the village court because its use is believed to have a calming effect on proceedings.<ref name="e18"/>

== Names ==
The alternate names for Numanggang are Boana, Kai, Manggang, Ngain, Numangan, Numangang, and Sugu.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.1 - Numanggang |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/numa1254 |access-date=2025-02-12 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref>

==The letter Ɋ==
The letter Ɋ, also known as [[Q with hook tail]], was introduced by Lutheran missionaries in Papua New Guinea for use in the Numanggang language in the 1930s or 1940s. In 2002, it was decided to discontinue using the letter.<ref>Lorna A. Priest, [https://www.unicode.org/L2/L2004/04348-phonetic.pdf Revised Proposal for Additional Latin Phonetic and Orthographic Characters], 2004</ref>
